newsitem.title: GREECE: BANK/GREECE SHOULD REDUCE RESERVE REQUIREMENTS-BANKER.
newsitem.headline: BANK/GREECE SHOULD REDUCE RESERVE REQUIREMENTS-BANKER.

text.p: The Bank of Greece should gradually reduce reserve requirements and obligatory re-deposits of foreign exchange by banks when monetary conditions are ripe, said Nikos Karamouzis, deputy governor of state National Bank.

"The Bank of Greece must, when monetary conditions allow it, present a programme of a gradual reduction of reserve requirements that are excessively high and continue to liberalize the foreign exchange that is deposited at the central bank," he said.

Karamouzis was speaking on the prospects and the problems of the banking system at a conference on the modernisation of Greece's banking and capital markets, organised by the Hellenic-American Chamber of Commerce and the Hellenic Bank Association.
The restrictions hurt the competitiveness of Greek banks, transfer jobs and banking services abroad and increase the cost of funding, he said.

The Bank of Greece imposes a 12 percent reserve requirement on bank liabilities to residents and non-residents and obliges credit institutions located in Greece to re-deposit 70 percent of the foreign exchange deposits with the central bank.

He added that Greek banks should formulate a medium-term strategy to cope with a changing international banking environment and this entailed heavy investments in risk management systems, new banking products and modern methods of internal audits.

He said that in the absence of major privatisations in the banking sector, state-run banks should have a top management that will ensure stability and continuity to bring this medium-term strategy to bear fruit.
Frequent changes of management at state banks at present and in the past have had negative consequences, he added.
Minority shareholders of state banks, especially insurance funds, should become more involved in appraising management performance and the results of the followed policies, he said.
The deputy governor of Greece's largest commercial bank said relations between state-run banks and the Greek state should not include preferential treatments.
